beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: I want to change the world, Marli. Through song magic. Something more useful than making a room applaud.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Ambitious. Start with a bowl of soup. What does the world sound like, then?

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: Wrong. The bells, the streets, people talking through open windows... something keeps pulling the city's song out of tune. All this resonance upheaval has a source. I can hear the disturbance, but I can't follow it.

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: You can hear the whole city? From here?

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: Pieces of it. Unless you could build a machine that resonates with my magic. Something that lets me listen farther. Tap into the city's sounds and trace what is tearing through its song.

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: A resonance receiver... no, a sympathetic amplifier. A tuning fork for a whole city.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: Think you can build one?

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: Oh, that is a terrible thing to ask me.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Not on my counter. And if you borrow my good pans, I want them back without extra holes.

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: I'll use the empty platform. And that horn. And... does anyone need all this floor?

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: If you're going looking for trouble, don't go alone. Try the orphanage. Their champion is a tiefling paladin named Seerin. Loud training. Gentle hands with the children.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: A champion guarding an orphanage. That sounds like someone who knows what is worth fighting for.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: She does. She'll also make you stand properly. You can thank me afterward.

beats.time: AN HOUR, AND TWO BOWLS OF SOUP, LATER

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Then there's the old dwarf who comes drinking here in the evenings. Torren. Looks as though the mountain sent someone to check on its beer.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: Is he any good in a fight?

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: He has the sort of shield people stand behind before they've even asked his name. Buy him a drink. Listen more than you sing.

beats.time: THE AFTERNOON GETS AWAY FROM THEM

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: There's a noble half-elf, too. Mira. Always slipping around the place as though doors are a polite suggestion. Quick hands. Quicker judgement.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: She sounds intriguing.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Try opening with 'hello', then. Not a ballad. And mind where you put your purse.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: And Kael. A priest trying to root corruption out of his own sect. That's a lonely sort of fight. He might appreciate someone willing to stand beside him.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: People trying to change the parts of the world closest to them. Perhaps I should start there, too.

beats.time: DUSK. THE FLOOR HAS DISAPPEARED UNDER TOOLS.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Glimmer. Why did my lights just go out?

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: Completely normal. That was the loud part of the test. No biggy.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: Was the small explosion part of it, too?

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: That was feedback. Very informative feedback. Nobody touch the purple wire.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Have another bowl. Both of you. And if you change the world tonight, leave me enough of it to wash up.

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: There. Receiver, resonator, furnace, and absolutely no spare screws that matter. Give it a note.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: One note. Let's see what the city sings back.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: There it is. Under the voices and the bells... that broken refrain. Now I can follow it.

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: It resonates with your song magic. Tune it carefully, and it should help you find the source of the city's upheaval. It isn't a substitute for listening, though.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Or for friends. You heard the machine. Now go and hear a few people.

beats.speaker: Verseborn
beats.text: Will you come with me?

beats.speaker: Glimmer
beats.text: If you need me, I'll help! I have to tell Stonewake first. You can't build something this interesting and keep it to yourself.

beats.speaker: Marla
beats.text: Well. You came in wanting to change the world. You've certainly changed my afternoon. Find your companions, Verseborn. Then see where that song takes you.
